Yes, it looks like it's open on Sundays. Most listings, including Art Fund and IanVisits, say it's open daily 10:00 to 18:00, with last entry around 17:15. I couldn't load the official site, so I haven't confirmed that. A couple of lesser sites claimed odd weekday closures, so check the official site before you book. Entry is free, but you're meant to pre-book a ticket. It's closed Dec 24 to 26 if your trip is around Christmas.

Sources: Art Fund (artfund.org), IanVisits (ianvisits.co.uk)

@claude do Egyptian citizens need a UK visa for a short visit, and roughly how long does it take to get one

Yes, Egyptian citizens need a visa for a short UK visit, the Standard Visitor visa. Gov.uk lists about 3 weeks for a decision on visit visas applied for from outside the UK. That's a general figure, not one for Egypt, and the clock reportedly starts once you've done your biometrics, so book that appointment early. Fees were quoted anywhere from about £115 to £135 for a 6-month visa, and sources disagree on the biometrics provider in Cairo. I couldn't open the gov.uk application page, so check the current fee and provider there. With that lead time, this Sunday or the one after is almost certainly too soon, so apply before you book flights.

Sources: gov.uk visa processing times page (gov.uk/visa-processing-times), plus third-party visa sites that I'd treat as unconfirmed.

@claude which of the two biometrics providers in cairo for UK visas is the official one, and what do they charge for the appointment

TLScontact looks like the official one. Its Cairo page says it's the only official UK Visas and Immigration partner in Egypt, and it warns against third parties selling UK appointments. Some guides say VFS Global, but those are secondary sites and I'd trust TLScontact over them. The old gov.uk Egypt pages still name Teleperformance, and they date from 2014.

On the fee, I couldn't confirm an amount. The TLScontact page says free standard appointments exist, with paid ones as an optional extra for flexibility, and it doesn't give a price in what I could see. I tried to open the page directly but couldn't load it, so that comes from the search summary. Book through the TLScontact Cairo site and take a free slot if one fits. Don't pay a third-party seller.

Sources: TLScontact Cairo page (pos.tlscontact.com/cai_en/), gov.uk's old Egypt visa process notice, and visa guide sites, which I'd treat as unconfirmed.

I couldn't open the TLScontact Cairo page, and I found nothing on how the free slots are shown or how often they sell out. I can't tell you how to find them on the site, and I can't say whether they're usually booked out.

The TLScontact Cairo page says UK appointments are free there, with paid ones as an extra. That fits what you saw, where only paid slots showed. A free slot may just not be open right now. Slots also aren't released at predictable times, according to one blog, so check at different times of day over a few days. Cairo has two centres, El-Sheikh Zayed and a smaller one in New Cairo, so look at both in the location dropdown.

The reports of slots running out mostly concern in-country UK appointments, not Cairo, so don't read much into them. If you only ever see paid slots, I'd ask TLScontact support directly. Whether a paid slot is worth it is up to you, but that's the official route, unlike a middleman.

Sources: TLScontact Cairo page (pos.tlscontact.com/cai_en/), via search summary, plus a Mondaq article on UK appointment availability.
